title: Rava bar Mechasya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Through him ten precious sayings of Rav remain to us. In Hyman’s citation of Shabbat 10b, Rava bar Mechasya said in the name of Rav Giddel, who spoke in the name of Rav.

(1) It is permitted to say “faith” in the privy. (2) One who gives a gift to his fellow must inform him. For this saying Rava bar Mechasya received two priestly gifts from an ox from Rav Chisda. Rava asked Chisda: “Are Rav’s teachings so dear to you?” Chisda answered, “Yes.” Rava said: “This is what Rav said: A garment is precious to its wearer.” Rav Chisda said: “Rav said this? The latter is better than the former; if I had another, I would give it to you.” (4) A person should not distinguish one son among the sons. (5) A person should always seek to live in a city that was recently settled. (6) Any city whose roofs are higher than the synagogue will in the end be destroyed. (7) Under an Ishmaelite and not under an idolater; under an idolater and not under a chaver, etc. (8) Any illness but not illness of the bowels; any pain but not pain of the heart; any ache but not an ache of the head; any evil but not an evil wife. (9) If all the seas were ink … they would not suffice to write the depths of government. (10) A fast is as good for a dream as fire for flax tow.
In Taanit 12b it reads Rabbah bar Chamsya.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1060) gives Rav Giddel as the middle link. The consulted text of Shabbat 10b–11a gives Rav Chama bar Guria, and Hyman also lists Shabbat 10b under Rav Chama bar Guria in his separate entry (vol. II, p. 459). The translation follows the reading in this entry.

The last line of Hyman’s printed entry and the consulted Taanit 12b read רבה בר מחסיא, “Rabbah bar Mechasya.” The supplied text has רבה בר חמסיא, “Rabbah bar Chamsya.” The consulted Shabbat passage has Rava.
